data.name: HomePageTitle
data.value: Workbench · Design, review and capture every page

data.name: HomeEyebrow
data.value: Part of your bit Boilerplate project

data.name: HomeHeadline
data.value: Finish the design before the backend exists.

data.name: HomeLead
data.value: The workbench runs your app's pages on sample data, so you can design every state, see it on every device and export store-ready screenshots, with the same components and theme your app ships with.

data.name: HomeFactNoServer
data.value: No API, database or sign-in needed

data.name: HomeFactStores
data.value: Exact App Store, Google Play and Microsoft Store sizes

data.name: HomeWhyTitle
data.value: Why your project has a workbench

data.name: HomeWhySubtitle
data.value: A design tool, a test bench and a photo studio for your pages, inside the project itself.

data.name: HomeWhyAgentsText
data.value: You don't need Claude Design or Figma. Whether you use Codex, Copilot or Claude Code, your agent can design pages here, look at them in a real browser and refine them.

data.name: HomeWhyRealText
data.value: Pages use the same bit BlazorUI components, theme and styles as your app, so what you approve here looks the same once it is built into the app.

data.name: HomeWhyStatesText
data.value: Loading, empty, error, partial and slow data are one click away, including the states that are hard to catch in a running app.

data.name: HomeWhyDevicesText
data.value: Phones, tablets and desktops at their real sizes, in light and dark, in every language your app supports.

data.name: HomeWhyStoresText
data.value: Export pixel-exact images at App Store, Google Play and Microsoft Store sizes, with a colored background and a caption when you want one, rendered by a real browser.

data.name: HomeWhyHeadStartText
data.value: It starts with ready-made pages, like a point-of-sale dashboard, a shift planner and your app's own settings page. Reuse what fits, learn from the rest, then add your own pages next to them.

data.name: HomeWhySafeText
data.value: Nothing here talks to your API or database, so trying a new idea never breaks your app or your data.

data.name: HomeWhyShareText
data.value: Send a link to a page in a given state to your team or client, and settle the design before anyone writes backend code.

data.name: HomeHowStep1Text
data.value: Build the page in the workbench with sample data that loads like the real thing.

data.name: HomeHowStep2Text
data.value: Check it on each device, theme, language and data state, one at a time or side by side.

data.name: HomeHowStep3Text
data.value: Rebuild the approved design in your app the way the rest of the app is built, and connect it to real data. Your AI agent follows the same steps.

data.name: HomePagesSubtitle
data.value: Start from these, then add your own pages next to them.

data.name: HomeFooter
data.value: The workbench is part of every bit Boilerplate project. It runs only on your machine unless you choose to publish it.
